Latent profile analysis

lpa.Rd

Fits a latent profile model (a finite mixture of multivariate normal distributions) to continuous indicators, with the within-profile variance and covariance structure chosen by variances and covariances.

Usage

lpa(
  data,
  items,
  K,
  variances = "equal",
  covariances = "zero",
  starts = c(100, 20),
  covariates = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  invariance = "full",
  device = "cpu",
  seed = 20261119,
  maxiter = 5000,
  tol = 1e-10,
  cluster = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  optseed = NULL,
  level2 = NULL,
  KB = NULL,
  between_covariates = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame or matrix; the indicators must be numeric.

items

Indicator columns (tidyselect). Default: all columns of data.

K

Number of classes (a positive whole number).

variances

Within-profile variances: "equal" across profiles (default) or "varying".

covariances

Within-profile covariances: "zero" (default), "equal" or "varying" (see Details).

starts

Length-2 integer vector: number of stage-1 random starts and of stage-2 starts iterated to convergence (Mplus STARTS). A single number is recycled. The default c(100, 20) with 20 stage-1 EM iterations corresponds to Mplus STARTS = 100 20; STITERATIONS = 20 (the Mplus defaults are 20 4 and 10 iterations).

covariates

Optional numeric covariates for a one-step latent class regression (Mplus c ON x): columns of data (tidyselect, e.g. c(age, female)) or a numeric data frame / matrix with one row per row of data. Needs K >= 2.

ref

Reference class of the latent class regression (default: the last class).

weights

Optional sampling weights: one column of data (e.g. w) or a numeric vector with one value per row; rescaled to sum to the number of analysed rows.

group

Optional known group for a multigroup model (Mplus KNOWNCLASS): one column of data (e.g. sex) or a vector with one value per row.

invariance

With group: "full" (measurement invariance, default), "none", or a character vector of indicator names whose parameters are group-specific (partial invariance). Ignored without group.

device

"cpu" (default) or "cuda" (NVIDIA GPU; needs CUDA.jl in the Julia environment).

seed

Random seed for the random starts.

maxiter

Maximum number of EM iterations in stage 2.

tol

Convergence tolerance: change in the log-likelihood per case.

cluster

Optional primary sampling units (PSUs) of a complex survey design (Mplus CLUSTER with TYPE = COMPLEX): one column of data (e.g. psu) or a vector with one value per row. Standard errors, the MLR scaling correction factor and the tests built on them (compare_models(), Wald tests of r3step(), bch(), dcat()) are then design-based: computed from PSU totals of the weighted scores. Estimates and the log-likelihood do not change. blrt() is not available (as in Mplus). Analysed rows may not have a missing value.

strata

Optional strata of the design (Mplus STRATIFICATION): one column of data or a vector. PSUs are nested in strata (equal cluster codes in different strata are different PSUs); without cluster every row is its own PSU. A stratum with a single PSU is kept, as in Mplus.

start

Optional start values: a fitted latentmix model of the same type and number of classes (for example a fit to other data, or with fewer random starts). EM then runs from its estimates only, without random starts (Mplus user starting values with STARTS = 0; the analogue of OUTPUT: SVALUES).

optseed

Optional start number: rerun only that random start (stage 1 and stage 2), the analogue of Mplus OPTSEED; see refit_start().

level2

Optional cluster (level-2 unit) of every row for a two-level model: one column of data (e.g. school) or a vector with one value per row. Rows with a missing cluster are not analysed. Needs KB.

KB

Number of between-level (cluster) latent classes of a two-level model.

between_covariates

Two-level models: cluster-level covariates, constant within each cluster; columns of data (tidyselect) or a numeric data frame / matrix. With KB they predict the between class (Mplus cb ON z); with random = "factor" the between factor (f ON w). covariates are then within-level covariates of the individual classes (cw ON x / c ON x).

Value

An object of class latentmix (see lca() for its components) with info$kind "LPA" (or "MGLPA" for a multigroup model).

Details

The structures correspond to the model names of the mclust package as follows:

variancescovariancesstructuremclust
"equal""zero"equal variances, local independence (Mplus default)EEI
"varying""zero"profile-specific variances, local independenceVVI
"equal""equal"one full covariance matrix for all profilesEEE
"varying""varying"profile-specific full covariance matricesVVV

Other combinations are rejected by the Julia package. Full covariance matrices are not available on the GPU. Two-level LPA (level2, KB; see lca()) supports "equal" and "varying" variances with covariances = "zero". Missing values, starts, covariates, weights and multigroup models work as described in lca(); with group, invariance names the indicators whose profile parameters are group-specific.

See also

lca(), profilemeans(), profilevariances(), profilecovariances(), classify(), lm_table().

Examples

data(wellbeing)
# \donttest{
# six health-behaviour and wellbeing indicators: are there distinct lifestyle profiles?
p <- lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 4, variances = "varying")   # VVI
#> Starting Julia ...
p
#> ━━ Latent profile analysis ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   4 profiles, 6 indicators, n = 1000
#>   Variances: profile-specific; indicators uncorrelated within profile
#>   Random starts: 100 / 20; best LL replicated 20 times
#> 
#> ── Fit ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Log-likelihood      -9995.712      AIC                   20093.425
#>   Free parameters            51      BIC                   20343.720
#>   Observations             1000      Sample-size adj. BIC  20181.742
#>   Best LL replicated    20 / 20      Entropy                   0.855
#>                                      Smallest class            10.0%
#> 
#> ── Class sizes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Class  Proportion  Modal n  Avg. posterior
#>   ──────────────────────────────────────────
#>   1           0.418      420           0.915
#>   2           0.266      268           0.912
#>   3           0.216      212           0.927
#>   4           0.100      100           0.925
#> 
#> ── Profile means ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Indicator  Class 1  Class 2  Class 3  Class 4
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   sleep        7.085    7.600    5.878    7.889
#>   activity     3.542    5.781    2.839    0.918
#>   fruitveg     2.974    4.385    2.429    1.964
#>   stress       6.089    3.292   11.098    8.676
#>   lonely       4.598    3.700    6.049    7.617
#>   lifesat      6.993    8.257    5.193    4.631
#> 
#> ── Variances ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Indicator  Class 1  Class 2  Class 3  Class 4
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   sleep        0.465    0.365    0.857    1.086
#>   activity     2.177    4.310    2.094    0.378
#>   fruitveg     1.330    1.480    0.881    0.828
#>   stress       3.338    2.253    4.741    6.091
#>   lonely       0.625    0.280    1.014    0.856
#>   lifesat      1.001    0.817    1.623    2.204
#> 
#>   summary() for standard errors · lm_table() to export · classify() for posteriors
profilemeans(p)   # e.g. short sleep (about 6 h) with high stress (about 11 of 16)
#>            class1   class2    class3    class4
#> sleep    7.085464 7.600044  5.877936 7.8894882
#> activity 3.541653 5.780687  2.839283 0.9176709
#> fruitveg 2.973951 4.385015  2.428910 1.9636675
#> stress   6.089048 3.291932 11.097546 8.6762339
#> lonely   4.598344 3.700244  6.049324 7.6170787
#> lifesat  6.992607 8.256812  5.192539 4.6306269
# full within-profile covariance matrices (VVV) for comparison
p_vvv <- lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 4, variances = "varying", covariances = "varying")
c(VVI = BIC(p), VVV = BIC(p_vvv))   # the extra correlations do not pay off in BIC
#>      VVI      VVV 
#> 20343.72 20451.02
